changed.what: Applied the note: KA-578 is a G3 row in N23-KA, so g3_metamorphic collects its entry, not g1. The gate is now measured by two cargo runs and recorded from both receipts (N38b-19's receipt set). Left, the g1 run would never collect KA-578 and GATE-CORTEX-06 could not be recorded in full.

Applied F-U23b-2's note. The trainer reads its default action law and discount rates from registries/defaults.toml (N23b-25) with the OPEN-CORTEX-2 label. A task's declaration or --action-law overrides them, and the unit test trainer_defaults_from_registry checks this. Left, the trainer would hard-code an undecided default, and N23a-35's check of the label would have nothing to read.

A campaign-class pretraining job with no approved envelope is refused at submission by the daemon's size classifier with FROB-REF-704 (convention 14; N32-REF row 704 names train.family's derived scope), not 761. 761 stays for an approved row that does not cover the estimate. Step 0, the acceptance criterion and the test pretraining_admitted_only_in_row now say so. Left, the test would assert a code the daemon never returns for that case.

The raw-checkpoint arm runs train start --init raw:<parent>, which N23a-14 refuses with FROB-REF-802 (pointer /init) when shapes differ. The script now expects that refusal and records the pair as 'raw warm start impossible'. Left, every topology pair would fail the script at a step the gate expects to be impossible.

The bead had no e2e script of its own (convention 11). Its test plan pointed at N23a-36's small-scale step, which does not measure GATE-CORTEX-14, and it scored the baseline teacher with eval run --policy <controller>, a form eval.run does not have. It now owns scripts/e2e/cortex_distill_experiment.sh: every run keyed, the teacher scored inside the job, the controls through N23b-15's forms, and the receipt printed for the recording session. Left, the gate could not be measured and the teacher evaluation would be refused.

Three fixes. (1) The symmetry-breaking control had no command, and under the default --group obs the verb refuses nothing, so the control could never be caught. It now runs --tying equivariant --group mech --dry-run and expects 161. (2) Arm M had no reachable command; it is now a feature-gated example labelled diagnostic-override. (3) New envelope rows take R29 onward (N44-01), not 'R19 onward' (R19 is reserved for KILL-ATLAS). Left, the control and arm M could not run, and a filed row would collide with a reservation.

check-contracts (N34-08) requires contract.toml and tests/conformance.rs in every workspace member, with every frontier-* feature naming its kill gate and pilot. The bead delivered neither file, so its own criterion could not pass. Added both: four frontier features (KILL-FAMILY, -INHERIT, -DISTILL, -EQUIV, with their pilots) and safe mode refuse:FROB-REF-702. Also added the deps N23b-16 and N34-08 and a planted control, and fixed 'check-contracts -p frob-learn' (the check takes no crate argument). Left, the crate fails its contract check and the kill-gate owner declarations have no file to go in.

N23a-35's rollout-storage step asserts padded worlds, charged copies and a storage digest 'in train.status', but no output carried them. The bead now defines RolloutAccounting, which N23a-14 reports as train.status's rollout block, and its e2e reads that block. Left, the step reads fields that do not exist, and the two-run storage comparison is impossible from the user's side.

The script gave each KA row a host entry plus one per device site. N23-KA gives KA-582 host only, and KA-586 host and lockstep. Corrected. Left, an implementer would look for, or report missing, entries the registry never defines.

Applied H-verbs-10: --init raw:<policy> (copy by position, manifest init: raw:<policy>, a shape mismatch is 802 at pointer /init), with a criterion and two unit tests. The refusals paragraph now matches the row: 161 and 726 come through hooks, and the worded and proposed refusals are raised through constants with no numbers written. --scenes <set> is spelled as the row spells it. Also added the train.status rollout block (N23a-06's accounting) with a test, and the deps N23a-06 and N23a-12. Left, BD-322's and N10b-15's raw arm had no input, and proposed numbers would be written as codes, against N35-33 rule 7.

GATE-CORTEX-08's parity part includes the 0.25 and 32/9 fixtures (g1 entries KA-587 and KA-588), but it was recorded from the g2 receipt alone. The script also ran the two fixtures as two g1 runs, and two receipts of one tier are refused by record_gate with receipt-set-invalid. It is now one g1 run filtered by the gate plus one g2 run, recorded with --receipt <g1> --receipt <g2>. Left, the gate record would miss its fixture clauses or be refused.

Applied F-U17a's note: frob phylum generate --locate answers a design outside the support with FROB-REF-541, exit 3 (N17a-20, its one raising site), not an ok result carrying a reason. The script now expects the refusal through e2e_expect_refusal FROB-REF-541 3, reads the reason from the refusal block and compares it with in_support. Left, the script would fail on every held-out design it is meant to locate.

Replaced the C13 narration ('requested of that row') with the fact: the policy.apply row of VERBS-policy spells --score-for-ladder select|discard, and a bare flag or any other value is the appended 802. Left, an implementer would read the flag as not yet defined and might choose another spelling or code.

Made the same C13 fix for --score-for-ladder. The margin unit test expected 'margin 22 percentage points', but the reported margin is a fraction of the box width. It now expects 22/60 = 0.367, above the 5% edge, so no near-support-edge flag. Left, the test's expected value was in a unit the report does not use.

Both train.family probes lacked --task-family, which the train.family row and BD-320's own probes pass. Added --task-family velocity. Left, the probes would be refused for the missing input instead of showing the kill gate's behaviour.

The e2e asserted two things on one fixture: the clean depth sequence (resets at the 6th and 12th steps) and a regression reset from a planted pair. A regression reset moves every later depth reset, so both cannot hold. It now runs two replays: audit-results, with every pair within 5%, for the depth sequence; and audit-results-planted for the regression reset, the inconclusive pair and the mixed-origin refusal. Left, the script would fail on a correct build.

The bead reset a lineage when the audit twin was 'more than 5% better', but N23a-28's rule is R_inh < 0.95*R_fresh, a different threshold: a twin 5.1% better gives R_inh = 0.951*R_fresh, which is no regression. The bead now states N23a-28's rule, and drop_triggers_reset checks 6% (reset), 4% and 5.1% (no reset). Left, the schedule's test and the mechanism would disagree at the boundary.

Applied H-ref-2's answer: tying-group-trivial is stated as N23-REF's late row 8, with its pointer, observed and required values and its repairs (1. --tying none; 2. frob analyze symmetry, remove the asymmetry). The repair '--tying augmentation' is removed: Gamma_aug is a subgroup of Gamma_obs, so on a trivial Gamma_obs augmentation is refused under the same slug. The C13 narration about the train.start row is gone, because the row lists --group and 161. The script step and the unit test now assert the repairs. Left, the refusal would advise a repair that itself fails.

Made the C13 fix: tying-group-trivial is N23-REF row 8, with observed group aug of order 1 and the same repairs. The script also read the symmetry residual, the elements and the update-cost multiplier from train.status, which had no such output, so the bead now extends train.status with an augmentation block. Left, the script's metrics had no source, and the refusal was narrated as pending.

Applied F-U23b-1's note in three parts. Rate fixtures: one task file per control rate (sim.run has no rate input), with KA-578 run in g3_metamorphic. Commands: check-contracts now runs without -p, and the spark check backends use the row's spellings mapped from E2E_DEVICES. Telemetry: --stream env is not one of the nine streams, so obs and final_obs are queried without --stream and terminated and truncated come from the task stream. Charged copies are read from the rollout block. Left, steps 1, 3, 4 and 11 would be refused or collect nothing, and KA-578's entry would never run.

Applied the notes from F-U23a-1 and F-U23b-2. Step 1 now follows N23a-06: two keyed runs, the rollout block, and masked-against-dense from the GATE-CORTEX-07 receipt. A dry run and the export manifest check the default action law with its label and beta 0.5025/s, kappa 2.565/s; an optional three-seed comparison does not block. The C13 narration about N35-06 is stated as fact. The battery and step 17 were already in the Gauntlet and convention-9 forms. Left, step 1 asked for a dense reference run no verb can build, and the default-law label had no check.

Made the C13 fix in step 4. Step 11's dry run and approved-envelope probe had no key and no approval input (train.family is a run verb); they now carry --key am-tf-dry, and --approval <token> --key am-tf-2. The code is now explained: 761 per BD-320's admission, since the 16-design job is below campaign class. Step 12 now says how the manifest and flags are read from artifact.read's bytes. Left, the probes would be refused for the missing key, and the manifest step had no defined way to read its fields.

The e2e's refusal dry runs had no expected codes, and the body called an oversized replay ring 'a budget refusal' (701 or 761, exit 4). They now expect 724 for the latent law and for a GRU (not admitted, rule 5 of VERBS-train's notes), and 602 for a ring over the device budget at admission. Left, the refusal steps could not fail, and an implementer might raise a budget code for a memory refusal.
The refusal dry runs had no expected codes. They now expect 724 for --tying equivariant with td3 (repair --tying augmentation) and for a GRU. Left, the refusal step could not fail.

Applied H-verbs-10's note: one change of this bead registers the predicate, enters the train.start row's needs_groups entry, and sets VERBS-train's needs_groups_es expectation with 790 in the generated list. The criterion was rewritten to match. The oversized-network refusal now expects 724, and cargo xtask check-deps is spelled in full. Left, the entry could be filed before its predicate (refused by needs-groups-known) or never, leaving 790 unreachable.

requests.what: KA-593 is listed as 'G1 · host', but N23ap1-01 and BD-255 run its entries on lockstep or batch-cpu, cuda and metal, and the row's carried-by text says 'on every backend'. Add those sites (host, lockstep, cuda, metal). Left, the Gauntlet collects only the host entry, and the device-side delay-ring checks never run as Gauntlet entries.

train.status's Outputs should list the block rollout (bytes_allocated, valid, invalid, padded_worlds, charged_copies and storage_digest of the last completed collection; N23a-06's RolloutAccounting, reported by N23a-14). Left, N23a-34's and N23a-35's steps read fields the row does not declare, and the row's schema test would reject them.

train.status's Outputs should list the block augmentation (symmetry_residual, elements_used, elements_dropped with reason, update_cost_multiplier; N23a-32, under --tying augmentation) beside the sac, td3 and es additions. Left, N23a-32's script reads fields the row does not declare.

The worded refusal tying-group-trivial is still described as 'N23-REF's request'. N23-REF now holds it as late row 8 (exit 3, pointer tying, repairs --tying none, then frob analyze symmetry). Cite the row. Left, the row and N23a-31/N23a-32 disagree on the refusal's status.

Step 2 says FROB-REF-704 is 'raised only by the daemon's scheduler at dispatch', and the test envelope_check_blocks maps 'no token' to 761 for any size. Convention 14 and N32-REF row 704 say the size classifier refuses a campaign-class job with no approved envelope for its scope at submission with 704, before envelope admission, and row 704 names train.family's derived scope. Split the case: a campaign-class estimate with no approved envelope gives 704; a smaller job above its scope's class in force, or an approved row that does not cover the estimate, gives 761. Left, BD-321 (now 704 for the full-scale job) and BD-320 assert different codes for one situation.
Line 77 says new envelope requests take 'R27 onward', but N44-01 reserves R12 to R28 and says new requests take R29 onward. Use R29. Left, a new request could be filed into reserved rows R27 or R28.

notes: Unchanged after a full read: BD-193, BD-196, BD-198, BD-255, N23a-03, N23a-05, N23a-10, N23a-12, N23a-13, N23a-15, N23a-16, N23a-17, N23a-18, N23a-20, N23a-21, N23a-27, N23a-30, N23a-33, N23ap1-01. Every slice note was checked and applied. The notes for N23a-37 and N23a-38 (drop eval run --battery cortex-offpolicy) and N23a-35's battery and step-17 parts were already done in the text; those beads were changed for other defects. Program-level matters left as they are: (1) Some gates have two recorders for split clauses, for example GATE-CORTEX-08: parity by N23a-19, two-card scaling by BD-199. (2) GATE-CORTEX-13 and -14 are measured by e2e scripts (BD-322, BD-323), not Gauntlet tiers, yet record_gate and the kill-decision scripts (N23a-30) read hash-named Gauntlet receipts; the receipt form of an e2e-measured gate is not defined anywhere I read. (3) N23a-13 stores a checkpoint at PolicyId = BLAKE3(manifest_digest || weights_digest), which is not BLAKE3 of the file's bytes, while artifact.read takes a b3: content digest. Whether the store resolves that alias address decides whether frob artifact read <policy_id> (N23a-13, N23a-36) works. (4) The measuring beads depend on N23b-16 (gate rows) and N23-KA only transitively, through the mechanism beads. graph_check finds every such path and 0 cycles, so no dep was added except N23a-01's. Helper: scratchpad polish-r4-F-U23a/check.py (front matter and result validation).
